text_1.text: Altera Agilex 5 devices serve a broad range of applications that require high performance, lower power, and smaller form factors. This tier consists of the performance-optimized D-Series FPGAs and the power-optimized E-Series FPGAs. Altera Agilex 5 devices also feature the industry’s first Enhanced DSP with AI Tensor Block, which deliver high-efficiency AI and digital signal processing (DSP) functionality, and the FPGA industry’s first asymmetric applications processor system consisting of dual Arm Cortex-A76 cores and dual Cortex-A55 cores, which enable you to optimize the performance and power efficiency of their workloads. These characteristics make them ideal for midrange FPGA applications across the edge and core including wireless and wireline communications, video and broadcast equipment, industrial applications, test and measurement products, medical electronics, and defense applications.

table_1.text:
E-Series FPGAs and SoCs D-Series FPGAs and SoCs
E-Series FPGAs and SoCs are optimized for power and size - with 50% lower power while delivering up to 2.5X better performance as compared to Cyclone V devices, also with features including transceiver rates up to 24x28 Gbps, PCIe 4.0x4, 6x25GbE, 3,600 Mbps DDR5, dual core of A55 and dual core of A76 make it ideal for intelligent applications at the edge, embedded, and more. D-Series FPGAs and SoCs are optimized for performance and power efficiency - with 42% lower power while delivering up to 1.5X better performance as compared to Stratix 10 FPGAs, also with features including transceiver rates up to 32x28 Gbps, PCIe 4.0x8, 16x25GbE, 4,000 Mbps DDR5, dual core of A55 and dual core of A76 make it ideal for various applications across multiple markets.

text_1.text:
What is the difference between Agilex 5 E-Series and D-Series?

E-Series is optimized for power and size: 50% lower power and up to 2.5× better performance than Cyclone V, transceivers to 24×28 Gbps, and PCIe 4.0 x4. D-Series is optimized for performance: 42% lower power and up to 1.5× better performance than Stratix 10, transceivers to 32×28 Gbps, and PCIe 4.0 x8.

What is the AI Tensor Block in Agilex 5?

Agilex 5 includes an Enhanced DSP with AI Tensor Block for high-efficiency AI and DSP. Peak INT8 throughput reaches 25.99 TOPS on the E-Series A5E 065A and 56.22 TOPS on the D-Series A5D 064, with variable-precision DSP blocks.

What processors are in the Agilex 5 hard processor system?

The SoC uses an asymmetric applications processor: dual Arm Cortex-A76 cores up to 1.8 GHz and dual Cortex-A55 cores up to 1.5 GHz, with up to 2 MB shared L3 cache. That pairing balances performance and power by workload.

Which memory and interface standards does Agilex 5 support?

DDR5 to 4,000 Mbps on D-Series and 3,600 Mbps on E-Series, plus DDR4, LPDDR4, and LPDDR5. Connectivity includes PCIe 4.0, up to 6×25GbE on E-Series and 16×25GbE on D-Series, MIPI D-PHY, LVDS at 1.6 Gbps, and TSN.

What applications is the Agilex 5 mid-range FPGA aimed at?

Midrange edge and core designs: wireless and wireline communications, video and broadcast, industrial, test and measurement, medical electronics, and defense. Named focus markets are image sensor processing, autonomous mobile robots, and clinical systems, including battery-powered clinical equipment.

text_1.text: The Altera Agilex 7 devices include the industry’s highest performance FPGAs providing a range of premium features for the most demanding applications, including the F-Series, I-Series, and M-Series. This tier offers the industry’s highest data rate transceivers - up to 116 Gbps - the first PCIe 5.0 and CXL support, and options to integrate in-package HBM2E memory delivering the industry’s highest memory bandwidth (over 1 TBps). These capabilities enable customized connectivity and acceleration for the most compute, bandwidth, and memory-intensive use cases in communications, data center, defense, high-performance computing, video, high-end test/measurement/medical, and more.

table_1.text:
F-Series FPGAs and SoCs I-Series FPGAs and SoCs M-Series FPGAs and SoCs
F-Series devices are general purpose FPGAs built on Altera 10 nm SuperFin process technology. With features including transceiver rates up to 58 Gbps, advanced digital signal processing (DSP) blocks supporting multiple precisions of fixed-point and floating-point operations. I-Series devices offer the highest performance I/O interfaces to address bandwidth-intensive applications. Manufactured on Altera 10 nm SuperFin process technology, this series builds upon the F-Series device features offering transceiver rates up to 116 Gbps, PCIe 5.0 support, and cache- and memory-coherent attach to processors with CXL. M-Series devices are optimized for compute and memory-intensive applications. Leveraging Altera 7 process technology, this series builds upon I-Series device features offering an extensive memory hierarchy including integrated high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and high-efficiency interfaces

text_1.text:
Altera Cyclone 10 is a family of field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) offering a low-power, cost-effective solution for various applications. The Cyclone 10 family includes two device families, Cyclone 10 LP, and Cyclone 10 GX, each optimized for different use cases.

The Cyclone 10 LP family is designed for low-power, cost-sensitive applications that require a balance of power and bandwidth. It features up to 220K logic elements, 6.4 Gbps transceivers, and 1,600 Mbps DDR3 memory support. It also offers integrated intellectual property (IP) such as ARM Cortex-M1 processor, analog-to-digital converter (ADC), and digital signal processing (DSP) blocks.

The Cyclone 10 GX family is optimized for high-performance applications that require higher bandwidth. It features up to 220K logic elements, 12.5 Gbps transceivers, and 2,666 Mbps DDR4 memory support. Altera Cyclone 10 also offers advanced processing capabilities with up to two ARM Cortex-A9 processors, hard floating-point DSP blocks, and a range of configurable I/O standards.

Overall, Altera Cyclone 10 FPGAs offer a versatile and flexible solution for various applications such as industrial automation, smart vision, and automotive. They provide low-power, cost-effective, and high-performance options that can be customized to meet specific requirements.

text_1.text:
Edge AI Sensor Aggregation Built for the Camera to GPU Pipeline

Modern edge AI vision systems demand more than compute power. Before an AI model can process a single frame, that frame has to get from sensor to GPU with minimal latency and zero data loss. Altera FPGAs solve this sensor aggregation challenge, pairing scalable I/O flexibility with deterministic, low latency streaming to feed NVIDIA's Holoscan platform.

Altera's FPGA based Edge AI sensor solutions combine scalable compute performance, PQC enabled security, and low latency deterministic AI inferencing for real time edge applications. Flexible I/O aggregates audio, video, SoC, and other interfaces for pre processing within the FPGA, then streams to external compute such as GPU or CPU.

Macnica Americas offers the Altera Agilex 5 development kits used in Altera's own Holoscan Sensor Bridge reference designs, giving your team a direct path from evaluation to production.

title_1.jcr:title: Why Altera FPGAs for Edge AI Sensor Bridging

text_1.text:
Scalable Performance Spectrum

Altera FPGAs span a broad range of features and performance, enabling Edge AI sensor bridge solutions from 1 to 400 Gbps. Whether the application calls for a single camera or a dense multi sensor array, there is an Agilex or Stratix device sized to fit.

Universal Sensor Interface Support

Altera FPGAs support the sensor interfaces Edge AI applications actually use in the field, including MIPI, JESD204, LVDS, SPI, CAN, HDMI, SDI, I2C, GPIO, and SLVS-EC. One FPGA platform, many sensor and video interface types.

Field Upgradeable Flexibility

Unlike fixed function ASIC, ASSP, or microcontroller based sensor bridges, an FPGA is field upgradeable. Hardware and software changes remain possible after deployment, protecting your investment as sensor requirements evolve.

Holoscan Sensor Bridge is built to serve any application where high bandwidth sensor data needs to reach GPU compute with minimal latency. Common deployments include:

Robotics & Sensor Fusion

Processes data from multiple sensor types, including lidar and radar, in real time, integrating seamlessly with FPGA-based I/O.

Live Media Production

Connects live, high-speed camera feeds with AI, enabling software-defined production switching and analysis. A natural fit alongside SMPTE ST 2110 IP-based production workflows.

Industrial Inspection

Enables real-time defect detection on production lines and continuous quality monitoring.

Medical Imaging

Supports AI-enabled medical devices, assisting with surgical visualization, body pose estimation, and real-time image processing such as enhanced endoscopy feeds.

Radar Signal Processing

Accelerates real-time radar data pipelines, including FFT-based processing.

6G & Software-Defined Radio

Connects analog sensors to GPU compute for efficient, low-latency signal processing.

title_1.jcr:title: Why Edge AI? The Case for Local Processing

text_1.text:
Cloud-based AI inference is facing real headwinds: bandwidth costs, ongoing service fees, latency constraints, data privacy regulations, and connectivity limitations in the field. The Ambarella N1 family is purpose-built for the shift toward edge-native AI, where the intelligence lives in the device rather than in a remote data center.

Ambarella’s CVflow® architecture and fine-tuning techniques, including QLoRA-based model compression, make it possible to run production-grade GenAI models in power-and-cost-constrained enclosures. The result is a new class of intelligent edge device that responds faster, costs less to operate, and is more secure by design.

The N1-655’s combination of multi-channel video decode, VLM support, and sub-20W power envelope makes it well suited for AMRs that need to interpret complex environments, respond to natural language commands, and operate continuously without a cloud connection.

From AI visual inspection to collaborative robots on the production line, the N1 family supports the multi-sensor, real-time processing that modern manufacturing requires. Both SoCs integrate naturally into AIoT architectures where data stays on the factory floor.

Process multiple camera feeds simultaneously, run object detection, classification, and tracking alongside VLM-based scene understanding, all within a single manageable power budget. Eliminate recurring cloud processing costs for large-scale deployments.

title_1.jcr:title: On-Premise AI Boxes and Edge Servers

text_1.text: For enterprises that cannot or will not send sensitive video and sensor data to the cloud, the N1 family enables full-featured GenAI inference to run locally in a standard rack, an industrial enclosure, or an edge appliance.

High-resolution imaging, real-time diagnostics support, and patient data that never leaves the facility. The N1’s processing depth and sensor fusion capabilities address the demanding requirements of edge medical AI.

textwithimage_1.text:
The ADPD4100/ADPD4101 operate as a complete multimodal sensor front end, stimulating up to eight light-emitting diodes (LEDs) and measuring the return signal on up to eight separate current inputs. Twelve time slots are available, enabling 12 separate measurements per sampling period.

The data output and functional configuration utilize an I2C interface on the ADPD4101 or a serial port interface (SPI) on the ADPD4100. The control circuitry includes flexible LED signaling and synchronous detection. The devices use a 1.8 V analog core and 1.8 V/3.3 V compatible digital input/output (I/O).

text_1.text:
The analog front end (AFE) rejects signal offsets and corruption from asynchronous modulated interference, typically from ambient light, eliminating the need for optical filters or externally controlled dc cancellation circuitry. Multiple operating modes are provided, enabling the ADPD4100/ADPD4101 to be a sensor hub for synchronous measurements of photodiodes, biopotential electrodes, resistance, capacitance, and temperature sensors. The multiple operation modes accommodate various sensor measurements, including, but not limited to, photoplethysmography (PPG), electrocardiography (ECG), electrodermal activity (EDA), impedance, capacitance, temperature, gas detection, smoke detection, and aerosol detection for various healthcare, industrial, and consumer applications.

The ADPD4100/ADPD4101 are available in a 3.11 mm × 2.14 mm, 0.4 mm pitch, 33-ball WLCSP and 35-ball WLCSP.

title_2.jcr:title: See New Possibilities in 120 MP Resolution

textwithimage_1.text: By incorporating close to the same number of pixels as photoreceptors in the human eye, the Canon 120MXS CMOS sensor delivers ultra-high 120 MP resolution in a compact design. At the same time, pixel-level innovations allow for faster readout speeds with lower noise ratios at 9.4fps - or higher when reducing the amount of readout lines. Uncover the finest details and find new clarity in industrial vision with the 120MXS CMOS Sensor from Canon. This 120-Megapixel CMOS sensor is available in monochrome (120MXSM), color (120MXSC), and with a specialized RGB-NIR color filter array (120MXSI).

text_1.text: By replacing one of the green filters on a standard color CMOS sensor with a Near Infra-Red (NIR) filter, image processing from this sensor allows for the separation of visible and NIR spectrums. Discrete analysis of these bands from a single image simplifies dual sensor systems by reducing size, weight, and power (SWaP) requirements, provides added capabilities to systems that can benefit from the additional band, and enhances current solutions already detecting in both the NIR and visible wavelengths such as precision agriculture with the benefit of 120MP resolution.

title_1.jcr:title: New Pixel Structure Advances High-Resolution Imaging

text_1.text: The Canon 120MXS CMOS sensor shares a Floating Diffusion Node between four pixels instead of one, allowing for smaller readout circuitry and larger photodiodes which allows for increased sensitivity. Small 2.2µm pixels leverage a wire layer to prevent crosstalk, contributing to superior image quality, while progressive pixel reading of 28 digital output channels deftly handles the enormous amount of data from 122 million effective pixels.

title_1.jcr:title: Unique Pixel Design Allows for Fast, Flexible Imaging at Ultra-High Resolutions

text_1.text: The Canon LI8020SA 250 MP CMOS sensor minimizes noise without sacrificing speed by sharing floating diffusion capacitance between multiple pixels, resulting in shrunken readout circuitry and larger photodiode sizes. The defect that stops your line is smaller than most cameras can resolve

Canon's LI8030SA puts 410 million pixels behind the lens, giving automated and robotic inspection systems the resolution to catch what conventional vision hardware misses, from a full wafer down to a single micro bump.

Sensor status: In development at Canon. Macnica is scoping early samples and design in timelines now. Contact us to get on the list.

As packaging goes 3D, the defects that matter go microscopic

Advanced GPU and AI chips now stack dies with HBM, larger logic, and dense interposers. Every TSV, RDL trace, and micro bump adds another point of possible failure, and one bad connection can take the whole package down. Panel and chip unit costs are high enough that zero failure is the only acceptable target, which means inspection has to cover every connection, not a sample of them.

Most vision systems trade resolution for speed, or speed for field of view. On a full wafer or a large format package, that tradeoff is exactly where defects hide.

textwithimage_1.text:
One capture, an entire panel, in focus

LI8030SA is a back illuminated, stacked CMOS sensor with a redesigned readout architecture, built specifically for applications where resolution and field of view can no longer be a tradeoff. The monochrome variant adds 4 pixel binning, so the same sensor can drop to 100MP at 24fps when throughput matters more than maximum detail.

title_2.jcr:title: 4K60 HDMI Input/Output FPGA Development Board for Real-Time Video Processing

textwithimage_1.text:
The iEB-KXU2 from i-Chips is a high-resolution FPGA development board designed for real-time image processing and video system prototyping. It supports up to four channels of 4K60 HDMI input and output, enabling engineers to rapidly develop and validate multi-stream video processing architectures.

Built on an AMD Kintex UltraScale FPGA and equipped with DDR4 frame memory, the iEB-KXU2 provides a flexible platform for implementing scaling, warping, compositing, and other advanced video processing functions.

text_1.text:
• 4K60 Multi-Channel HDMI I/O: Supports 4 × HDMI 2.0 inputs and 4 × HDMI 2.0 outputs, each up to 4K60 resolution.
  • High-Performance FPGA Platform: Powered by AMD Kintex UltraScale FPGA for high-speed image processing and custom video pipeline development.
  • Integrated Frame Memory: On-board DDR4 memory enables temporal image processing and buffering for advanced video applications.
  • Flexible Control Options: Supports control via external PC (USB) or on-board microcontroller, selectable via DIP switch.
  • Simplified Development Environment: Includes register compiler and control tools to accelerate development without needing to build peripheral interfaces.

The iEB-KXU2 is designed as a flexible development platform for engineers building advanced video processing systems. It enables rapid prototyping of real-time image processing circuits using a high-performance FPGA architecture combined with multi-channel HDMI interfaces.

By integrating video input/output, frame memory, and control logic on a single board, the iEB-KXU2 allows developers to focus on implementing core processing algorithms such as scaling, warping, compositing, and format conversion without needing to design supporting hardware.

This makes it an ideal platform for early-stage system development, proof-of-concept validation, and evaluation of i-Chips video processing architectures.

text_1.text: i-Chips Scaler LSI (Large-Scale Integration), revolutionizes electronic devices by integrating numerous electronic components and functions onto a single chip. This advanced technology enables significant miniaturization and improved performance. In the context of video processing, the term "scaler" refers to the integrated circuit's capability to perform scaling or resizing functions. Found in TVs, monitors, projectors, and video processors, i-Chips Scaler LSIs convert incoming video signals to different resolutions, ensuring compatibility with various display formats. By leveraging sophisticated algorithms and signal processing techniques, i-Chips Scaler LSI large scale integration circuits analyze and modify video signals, upscaling or downscaling them to match the desired resolution or aspect ratio of the display device. Additionally, these chips may undertake additional tasks like deinterlacing, color space conversion, and noise reduction. i-Chips Scaler LSIs help in achieving optimal picture quality and seamless compatibility across different video sources and displays. They empower users to enjoy diverse video formats and resolutions on devices with varying display capabilities, providing an immersive visual experience.

  • Video Processing: Video processing systems, enabling format conversion, image enhancement, and manipulation in applications such as video broadcasting, video conferencing, surveillance, and professional video editing

title_2.jcr:title: Multi-modal 3D facial recognition for secure, privacy-compliant access control

text_1.text: NAMUGA is a global innovator in advanced camera modules and 3D sensing solutions, delivering ultra-compact, high-performance imaging technologies for some of the world’s most demanding applications. Founded in 2004 and headquartered in South Korea, NAMUGA combines advanced optics, sensing, AI-enabled imaging, and automated manufacturing expertise to help customers accelerate intelligent vision system development.

Vicon Lite is a vision-powered access control terminal developed by Namuga, drawing on more than 20 years of camera and sensing module expertise. Where conventional access control relies on cards, PINs, or centralized biometric databases, Vicon Lite replaces that model with multi-modal 3D facial recognition, on-device AI processing, and post-quantum encryption, delivering fast, accurate, and privacy-respecting authentication at the door.

Built on Namuga's NEPS platform, Vicon Lite brings together four capabilities that most access control systems treat as separate problems: strong biometric authentication, data sovereignty for the user, quantum-resistant security for data in transit and at rest, and plug-and-play deployment into existing RFID infrastructure. The result is a single compact terminal that handles every access challenge without added complexity or facility downtime.

Macnica Americas is an authorized distributor of Namuga and Vicon Lite in North America, providing customers with local technical support, system integration guidance, and access to Namuga's engineering resources.
Vicon Lite unifies the security, privacy, and deployment requirements that typically require multiple systems into a single compact terminal.

image_1.alt: Namuga Pinocchio dual-lens stereo depth RGB/IR camera banner

text_1.text: Vicon Lite uses stereo RGB and IR cameras to cross-validate depth, skin, and blood flow in real time. Photos, videos, and masks do not pass. The system achieves 99.7% recognition accuracy with a 0.3-second authentication speed, and supports facial vein recognition and gesture-based multi-factor authentication in the Pro model.

title_1.jcr:title: Post-Quantum Encryption via the NEPS Platform

text_1.text: Every layer of the Vicon Lite system is protected by the NEPS platform: ML-DSA and AES-256 encryption, PUF-based device key enclave for hardware-level protection, and TLS 1.3 for secure communications. This architecture provides protection against both current and emerging cryptographic threats, and is GDPR and CCPA compliant by design.

Biometric data never enters a central server. Vicon Lite uses a Self-Sovereign Identity architecture in which users carry their own encrypted identity. Users can enroll, update, or delete their biometric data at any time, giving individuals direct control over their own credentials. On-device 1:1 matching is the default mode, with 1:N matching available for enterprise deployments.

Vicon Lite integrates with any existing RFID environment in hours. No new wiring, no additional software installation, and zero facility downtime during deployment. A built-in web server handles device management without requiring separate software, and the system supports 1:1, 1:N, and hybrid authentication modes.

title_1.jcr:title: One Device. Every Access Challenge Solved.

text_1.text: Vicon Lite addresses three categories of access control challenge that traditional systems handle inadequately:

image_1.alt: Namuga Stella180 Solid State On-Device LiDAR banner

text_1.text: From the hardware key enclave to the cloud, every layer of the Vicon Lite system is protected by post-quantum encryption. Identity data in storage and in transit is secured against both present-day attacks and future cryptographic threats, making Vicon Lite future-proof from day one.

A single tap on a smartphone authenticates a user instantly via secure Bluetooth. No setup, no PIN, no physical card. The mobile ID capability leverages secure Bluetooth connection for biometric mobile access, reducing both friction and credential management overhead.

All facial recognition and anomaly detection runs directly on the Vicon Lite device. There is no cloud dependency, no recognition latency from round-trip processing, and no biometric data leaving the premises. The on-device AI also supports anti-tailgating analysis, detecting suspicious access behavior through AI-based behavior analysis.

Precision Network Synchronization for IEEE 1588/PTP

SiTime’s network synchronizers support nanosecond-level synchronization in distributed systems, enabling accurate timing across communications infrastructure - even under harsh environments and variable conditions.

title_2.jcr:title: Nanosecond Accuracy, MEMS Reliability, Network-Wide Timing Confidence

text_1.text: As next-gen networks demand tighter timing across distributed architectures, the TimeSync™ Platform from SiTime delivers industry-leading precision and robustness for IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP), Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE), and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) holdover. Unlike traditional quartz-based synchronizers, TimeSync™ integrates MEMS oscillators, DPLLs, and hitless switching logic in a compact, programmable device - resulting in superior resilience, smaller footprint, and longer holdover performance, even in harsh or mobile environments.

• Integrated DPLL + MEMS Oscillator: Combines digital phase-locked loop with rugged MEMS timing for sub-microsecond alignment under variable network conditions
  • Hitless Reference Switching: Maintains continuous, undisturbed operation during timing source transitions or failures
  • Precision Holdover: Maintains network sync with nanosecond-level accuracy even during GNSS loss, ideal for edge and indoor deployments
  • Multi-Protocol Support: Supports full Synchronous Ethernet and IEEE 1588 PTP timing stacks for a variety of telecom and datacom standards
  • Compact Footprint: Designed for space-constrained systems including small cells, fronthaul gateways, microwave backhaul, and C-RAN infrastructure
